prompt: HTTP/2 intermediary padding DATA vs HEADERS PUSH_PROMISE
answer:
HTTP/2 treats intermediary handling differently:

- **DATA padding:** Intermediaries **SHOULD maintain** it. The entire DATA payload—including the Pad Length and padding—is subject to flow control ([RFC 9113, §6.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9113.html)).
- **HEADERS and PUSH_PROMISE padding:** Intermediaries **MAY pass it through, re-pad it, or remove it**. These frames are not flow-controlled; excessive padding can block other streams similarly to a large header block ([HTTP/2 issue #505](https://github.com/httpwg/http2-spec/issues/505)).

The padding format and sender/receiver requirements for HEADERS and PUSH_PROMISE were later stated explicitly: padding must be zero when sent, and a receiver may treat non-zero padding as a `PROTOCOL_ERROR` ([RFC 9113, §§6.2 and 6.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9113.html)).
